ORAL JUDGMENT  Date: 19-07-2017  Heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as learned  Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
2. In all the three applications the petitioner has challenge  order taking cognizance dated 03.01.2011 in identical fact situation on the  complaint lodged at the instance of Food Inspector, Purnea.

Hence, all the three  applications are heard together as common question of facts and laws are  involved in all three cases.
 3. In all the three cases samples of edible oils were col  for examination of the Public Analyst about the purity in the edible oil.

In all  three cases the petitioner has raised the issue of violation of mandatory provis  as contained in Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (
 hereinafter to be referred to as the Act) which reads as follows:-

"13. Report of Public Analyst-  (2) On receipt of the report  of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to  the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the  Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution  of prosecution against the persons from whom the  sample of the article of food was taken and the  person, if any, whose name, address and other  particulars have been disclosed under section 14-A,

was collected from business premises of the petitioner on 04.12.2010.
The report  of the analysis was received on 08.01.2011.

In terms of Section 13 (2) of the Ac  the authorities under the Act was required to send the second sample of the edib  oils for the analysis to the Central Food Laboratory if the person from whose  premise the sample was collected and adverse analysis report was received and  communicated expresses desire and makes an application to the court within 10  from the date of receipt report for getting the 2nd sample of the article of Foo  kept by the Local (Health) authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory.
The avowed object of the Scheme under Section 13 (2) of the Act was to ensure  that the sample of the alleged adulterated food on analysis or reanalysis  established food adulteration.
The mandatory requirement of Section 13 (2) of th  Act
was to provide one more opportunity to the person against whom there is  adverse report in the first analysis to prove that the food item is not adultera

 5.

The case of the petitioner is that despite the reques  petitioner in terms of Section 13 (2) the second sample was not sent for analysi  by the authorities prescribed under the Act and, as such, the entire prosecution  based on the basis of prosecution report not supported by the analysis of second  sample is unsustainable and as such, the proceeding against the petitioner is cl  abuse of the process of law.

The petitioner specifically has pleaded that the li  the sample (edible oil) sent for analysis by the public analyst is one year and   sample was collected on 04.12.2010 and till the date of filing of the case on  Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.20424 of 2014 dt.19-07-2017  4/5  28.04.2014 the second sample could not be analysed and, as such, the prosecution against the petitioner is liable to be quashed on account of the non-compliance of the mandatory provision of Section 13 (2) of the Act.
6. Counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance of the Judgment of this court in the case of Sharwan Kumar Vs. The State of Bihar and reported in 1997 (1) PLJR 453 wherein a Bench of this Court relying upon the Judgment of the apex Court reported in A.I.R. 1991 suppl. (2) SCC 569 has held out that the order taking cognizance is bad and in the absence of second analysis report from the Central Food Laboratory in terms of Section 13 (2) the prosecution is unsustainable.
7.

No.10951 of 2001 and analogous cases dated 10.01.2012 to substantiate his argument that the order taking cognizance in the absence of report of the Central Food Laboratory in terms of Section 13 of the Act is unsustainable.
8. Counsel for the petitioner submits that the case of the petitioner is covered by the Judgment of the Apex Court mentioned above.

If Section 13 (2) of the Act mandates sending of second sample for the analysis of the Central Food Laboratory on the protest by the person against whom the first Mukesh Kumar Agrawal vs The State Of Bihar on 19 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98629734/
4 analysis report is received, then no prosecution can be lodged in absence of taking recourse to sending the second sample collected by the Food Inspector by the analysis of the Central Food Laboratory.

9. In identical facts situation the apex court has quashed the Patna High Court Cr.Misc. No.20424 of 2014 dt.19-07-2017 prosecution considering the mandate of the law in the case of Girish Bhai Dangra Bhai Sah vs. C.C.Jani & anr. reported in (2009)15 SCC 64.
10.

sentences.text: I find substance in the submission of the counsel for the petitioner and considering the binding precedent on this issue as discussed above, I am left with no option but to quash the order taking cognizance dated 03.01.2011 passed in all the three cases Complaint Case viz Complaint Case No.B-III-11/2011, Complaint Case No.B-III-07/2011 and Complaint Case No.B- III-08/ 2011 are quashed.
Accordingly, all the three cases are allowed.
